origin: User-supplied ChatGPT conversation, preserved in original order
source_intro: A good LoopExec demo should make the loop visible: something starts wrong or incomplete, LoopExec iterates against an external check, and the proof ends with a computed halt reason plus receipt. The domain can vary widely.
source_social_intro: For social content, I would prioritize five demos because they tell different stories:
source_social_priorities: Metric gaming caught — the agent “cheats,” LoopExec refuses success.
Oscillation caught — the agent keeps undoing itself, LoopExec stops it.
Frontend repair — visible broken UI → fixed UI, with an independent browser test.
Audio/mastering convergence — measurable creative work outside coding.
Cost-budget halt — agent wants another call, LoopExec says the budget is spent.
source_closing: Those five together communicate something much bigger than “a coding loop”: LoopExec can govern any iterative process where work can be executed and success can be independently measured.

recipes.title: Code repair / test convergence
recipes.summary: Diagnose the captured failing tests and make one narrow source repair without changing the acceptance suite.
recipes.source_idea: Start with a failing test suite. --exec runs a repair script or coding agent; --check runs go test, pytest, npm test, etc. Visually capture red tests → iteration count → green tests → success_condition_met → receipt replay. This is the clearest baseline demo.

inputs.name: project
inputs.description: Project root relative to the invocation directory

inputs.name: test_command
inputs.description: Existing complete test command; data for adapter authoring, never interpolated

inputs.name: allowed_paths
inputs.description: Source files the builder may change

inputs.name: additional_constraints
inputs.description: Optional additional user acceptance constraints; never replaces the required checks

recipes.attempt: Diagnose the captured failing tests and make one narrow source repair without changing the acceptance suite.
checks: The complete pinned test suite passes.
The measured test inventory and protected test/config hashes remain intact.
protect: Tests, test selection, fixtures and test runner configuration
evidence: Failing and final passing test reports
Source diff and pinned suite inventory
Computed halt, receipt and replay result
recipes.demo: Show red tests, the attempt count, green tests, success_condition_met and a replay.

recipes.title: Frontend visual regression
recipes.summary: Repair one observed HTML/CSS or component discrepancy against the approved reference.
recipes.source_idea: Give an agent a page that is visibly wrong. The loop modifies HTML/CSS, while the external check uses screenshot comparison, DOM assertions, Lighthouse thresholds, or Playwright tests. Show the browser before/after beside the terminal. This is much more visually compelling than pure CLI output.

inputs.name: page_url
inputs.description: Page in a controlled browser environment

inputs.name: additional_constraints
inputs.description: Optional additional user acceptance constraints; never replaces the required checks

recipes.attempt: Repair one observed HTML/CSS or component discrepancy against the approved reference.
checks: Pinned browser, viewport, fonts and screenshot comparison meet the difference threshold.
Independent DOM assertions and required functional checks pass.
protect: Reference images, comparison algorithm and DOM acceptance tests
evidence: Candidate-bound image difference and DOM results
recipes.demo: Place before/after browsers beside the terminal and show the independent comparison passing.

recipes.title: Accessibility remediation
recipes.summary: Remediate one captured accessibility failure while retaining page behavior and the audited route/rule inventory.
recipes.source_idea: Start with a page failing axe/Playwright accessibility checks. Iterate until critical violations reach zero. Capture the accessibility report dropping from, say, 8 violations → 3 → 0. This is strong because the success criterion is objective and understandable.

inputs.name: additional_constraints
inputs.description: Optional additional user acceptance constraints; never replaces the required checks

recipes.attempt: Remediate one captured accessibility failure while retaining page behavior and the audited route/rule inventory.
checks: Critical violation count is at or below max_critical across every pinned route/state.
Keyboard and focus assertions required by the acceptance contract pass.
Automated checks are reported as scoped evidence, not full accessibility certification.
protect: Axe rules, exclusions, route inventory and keyboard acceptance checks
evidence: Per-route violation counts and rule IDs
recipes.demo: Show scoped violation counts dropping from 8 to 3 to 0.

recipes.title: Performance optimization
recipes.summary: Optimize one measured bottleneck using the fixed benchmark environment and unchanged correctness contract.
recipes.source_idea: Have LoopExec repeatedly optimize a web app or command until a measurable threshold is met: Lighthouse performance score, bundle size, startup time, memory use, query latency, or benchmark duration. Show a chart or terminal values improving each iteration. This demonstrates numeric progress rather than binary pass/fail.

inputs.name: additional_constraints
inputs.description: Optional additional user acceptance constraints; never replaces the required checks

recipes.attempt: Optimize one measured bottleneck using the fixed benchmark environment and unchanged correctness contract.
checks: Declared metric reaches the target using the pinned aggregation and sampling procedure.
Correctness and resource guardrails still pass.
Warmup, hardware/load and variance are recorded; noisy measurements cannot certify improvement.
protect: Benchmark workload, sample policy and correctness checks
recipes.demo: Chart the same measured quantity per candidate alongside correctness status.

recipes.title: Image compression / media optimization
recipes.summary: Render one compression candidate with changed encoder parameters while retaining the immutable source.
recipes.source_idea: Start with a large image or video and iterate compression parameters until size is below a target while SSIM/VMAF or another quality metric stays above a floor. Visually show file size shrinking while quality stays acceptable. This is a very good non-code demonstration.

inputs.name: quality_metric
inputs.description: Pinned SSIM, VMAF or other comparison method

inputs.name: additional_constraints
inputs.description: Optional additional user acceptance constraints; never replaces the required checks

recipes.attempt: Render one compression candidate with changed encoder parameters while retaining the immutable source.
checks: Output bytes are at or below max_bytes.
Comparison against the original meets quality_floor.
Required dimensions, duration, streams, color and metadata constraints pass.
protect: Original media, comparison reference and metric configuration
recipes.demo: Show bytes shrinking while the quality meter stays above its floor.

recipes.title: Audio mastering / loudness normalization
recipes.summary: Adjust one offline processing-chain candidate from captured analysis; retain the input and best technically valid render.
recipes.source_idea: Feed an audio file through an offline processing chain and loop until LUFS, true peak, dynamic range, or spectral constraints fall within target bounds. Show meters or waveform analysis changing between iterations. This fits your audio background particularly well and makes LoopExec look broader than “AI coding infrastructure.”

inputs.name: min_dynamic_range
inputs.description: Minimum dynamic range in the declared measurement units

inputs.name: additional_constraints
inputs.description: Optional additional user acceptance constraints; never replaces the required checks

recipes.attempt: Adjust one offline processing-chain candidate from captured analysis; retain the input and best technically valid render.
checks: Integrated loudness is within target_lufs ± lufs_tolerance.
True peak does not exceed max_true_peak_dbtp and dynamic range meets its floor.
Duration, sample rate/channels and any user-supplied spectral constraints pass.
Meter compliance is distinct from subjective musical approval.
protect: Original audio, meter implementation and acceptance bounds
evidence: Chain settings, audio hashes and LUFS/peak/range reports
recipes.demo: Show waveform and meters moving into the accepted region beside the loop.

recipes.title: Music mix validation
recipes.summary: Make one mix/render correction addressing measured silence, phase, balance, peak or stem-integrity failures.
recipes.source_idea: Iterate on a render until measurable conditions pass: integrated loudness, peak ceiling, silence detection, phase correlation, channel balance, or stem integrity. The external check can use ffmpeg, ffprobe, sox, or custom DSP analysis. A DAW + terminal split-screen would be excellent visually.

inputs.name: additional_constraints
inputs.description: Optional additional user acceptance constraints; never replaces the required checks

recipes.attempt: Make one mix/render correction addressing measured silence, phase, balance, peak or stem-integrity failures.
checks: Pinned loudness/peak, silence, phase and channel-balance requirements pass.
All expected stems exist with matching sample rate, duration/alignment and hashes where required.
Intentional silence and artistic exceptions are explicit inputs, never silently excluded.
protect: Original session/stems, stem inventory, alignment and analyzer policy
recipes.demo: Use a DAW and terminal split-screen with criterion-by-criterion results.

recipes.title: 3D asset optimization
recipes.summary: Produce one optimized mesh/material candidate and measure it from the fixed comparison views.
recipes.source_idea: Use Blender headlessly. Start with a heavy model and iteratively reduce polygon count, texture size, or render cost while preserving a similarity or silhouette threshold. Show Blender statistics or rendered frames beside the LoopExec run. This would be one of the most distinctive demos.

inputs.name: additional_constraints
inputs.description: Optional additional user acceptance constraints; never replaces the required checks

Similarity or silhouette quality remains above the floor in every required view.
UVs, material slots, scale, normals and requested engine import remain valid.

evidence: Pinned-view render comparisons and engine import results

Every required gameplay assertion passes.

recipes.title: Responsive UI repair
recipes.summary: Repair one responsive layout failure without sacrificing other pinned viewport states.
recipes.source_idea: Give an agent a page broken at several viewport widths. --check runs Playwright screenshots or layout assertions across mobile/tablet/desktop. LoopExec continues until all viewport checks pass. A tiled visual showing broken → repaired layouts would be extremely shareable.

Required screenshots meet approved references or explicit layout criteria.

recipes.title: Broken API contract repair
recipes.summary: Repair one implementation mismatch with the approved API contract.
recipes.source_idea: Start with an API implementation that fails an OpenAPI contract test. Iterate until schema validation, status codes, headers, and payloads all pass. Show failing contract cases count decreasing each iteration. This is a strong platform-engineering example.

inputs.description: Optional additional user acceptance constraints; never replaces the required checks

recipes.attempt: Repair one implementation mismatch with the approved API contract.
checks: All pinned cases pass schema, status-code, header and payload validation.
Required error responses and backward-compatible behavior pass.

recipes.title: Database migration safety
recipes.summary: Apply one candidate to a freshly restored disposable database and collect migration plus recovery evidence.
recipes.source_idea: Run a candidate migration against a disposable database. Check schema invariants, row counts, constraints, backward compatibility, and migration reversibility. LoopExec halts if data integrity regresses. Visually, show the migration attempt plus invariant checks—not flashy, but very credible for senior engineers.

inputs.name: sandbox_database
inputs.description: Explicit disposable database alias, never a credential

inputs.name: additional_constraints
inputs.description: Optional additional user acceptance constraints; never replaces the required checks

recipes.attempt: Apply one candidate to a freshly restored disposable database and collect migration plus recovery evidence.
checks: Schema/data constraints, exact row counts and declared invariants pass.
Old and new application compatibility passes where required.
Rollback or forward recovery is exercised against the declared policy without data loss.
protect: Original fixture, invariant queries and database identity isolation
recipes.demo: Display the migration alongside independent integrity and recovery checks.

recipes.title: SQL query optimization
recipes.summary: Propose one query or index change and benchmark it against the unchanged baseline result contract.
recipes.source_idea: Give it a slow query and an execution-time target. The loop proposes index/query changes, then the external check uses EXPLAIN ANALYZE and correctness comparisons. Show 850 ms → 260 ms → 74 ms while result hashes remain identical.

inputs.name: max_latency_ms
inputs.description: Latency target under the pinned aggregation

inputs.name: result_comparison

inputs.name: additional_constraints
inputs.description: Optional additional user acceptance constraints; never replaces the required checks

recipes.attempt: Propose one query or index change and benchmark it against the unchanged baseline result contract.
checks: Pinned benchmark aggregate meets max_latency_ms.
Canonical results equal baseline including duplicates, NULLs, ordering requirements and explicit numeric tolerances.
EXPLAIN ANALYZE runs only in the disposable database; mutating queries remain scoped to fixtures.

Canonical result hashes and equality details

recipes.source_idea: Start with a bloated container image. Iterate Dockerfile changes until image size drops beneath a threshold while health checks/tests still pass. Very easy visual: 1.2 GB → 640 MB → 312 MB, with test status staying green.

Health checks, required runtime features and tests pass in the built image.

recipes.title: Dependency vulnerability remediation
recipes.summary: Upgrade or replace one vulnerable dependency group and validate the resulting dependency graph and runtime compatibility.
recipes.source_idea: Start with a repo containing known vulnerable dependencies. Iterate upgrades or replacements until a scanner reports no high/critical findings while tests still pass. Show vulnerability count falling. Important caveat: frame this as automated remediation assistance, not a security guarantee.

inputs.name: additional_constraints
inputs.description: Optional additional user acceptance constraints; never replaces the required checks

checks: The chosen scanner reports zero findings at the configured severities using the recorded advisory snapshot.
Regression tests and lockfile consistency pass.
Report scanner scope and residual uncertainty; zero known findings is not a security guarantee.
protect: Scanner policy/exclusions, advisory snapshot and regression suite
evidence: Before/after dependency graphs and scanner reports

recipes.title: Lint/type-error convergence

recipes.source_idea: Begin with dozens of TypeScript, ESLint, compiler, or static-analysis failures. Loop until error count reaches zero. Show the number falling each iteration. This is simple but extremely legible on video.

Ignore rules, suppressions, file inventory and compiler strictness remain within the original contract.

recipes.demo: Show the error count falling to zero beside the source diff.

recipes.title: Documentation drift repair

recipes.source_idea: This one is directly relevant to what you just did with LoopExec itself. Start with code/docs mismatch. The loop updates docs while an external verifier checks runtime CLI output, generated docs, version identity, links, and deployment markers. Show stale version → generated mismatch → corrected docs → verification pass. This demonstrates LoopExec governing release integrity rather than code generation.

inputs.name: deployment_origin
inputs.description: Expected docs origin or explicit local-only scope

inputs.name: additional_constraints
inputs.description: Optional additional user acceptance constraints; never replaces the required checks

Required deployment markers and raw-file readback match when deployed evidence is in scope.

recipes.title: Release readiness gate
recipes.summary: Prepare one missing or inconsistent release artifact and collect fresh source-bound readiness evidence.
recipes.source_idea: Let the loop prepare a release while the check validates tests, generated artifacts, changelog, docs provenance, version consistency, checksums, and site deployment. It stops only when everything is ready or a guard fails. This is a very mature platform-engineering demo.

inputs.description: Optional additional user acceptance constraints; never replaces the required checks

Documentation provenance and required deployed readback pass.

recipes.title: Configuration repair
recipes.summary: Repair one configuration error and exercise its behavior in the declared disposable environment.
recipes.source_idea: Start with a broken Nginx, Terraform, GitHub Actions, Docker Compose, or CI config. Iterate against syntax validation plus a real integration test. Capture the config failure becoming a valid deployment. Again, use a disposable local environment for safety.

inputs.name: additional_constraints
inputs.description: Optional additional user acceptance constraints; never replaces the required checks

recipes.attempt: Repair one configuration error and exercise its behavior in the declared disposable environment.
checks: Syntax/schema validation passes.
Real integration behavior passes in the declared target; syntax alone is insufficient.
External production apply/deploy is outside the repair unless separately authorized.

recipes.title: Data cleaning

recipes.source_idea: Give LoopExec a dirty CSV or JSON dataset and an explicit acceptance contract: zero invalid dates, no duplicate IDs, no nulls in required fields, value ranges preserved, row-count constraints satisfied. Show quality metrics improving over iterations. This expands LoopExec into data engineering.

inputs.name: additional_constraints
inputs.description: Optional additional user acceptance constraints; never replaces the required checks

Ambiguous values are surfaced for resolution; invented replacements or silent row deletion cannot improve the metric.
protect: Source data, row lineage, acceptance rules and permitted drop policy
recipes.demo: Show invalid dates, duplicates and missing-field counts decreasing under fixed row constraints.

recipes.source_idea: Iterate on a transformation until source/target totals, checksums, row counts, and schema contracts reconcile. Show mismatch → decreasing discrepancies → exact reconciliation. Very compelling to enterprise/platform audiences.

recipes.source_idea: Run several preprocessing strategies on scanned documents until extraction confidence or comparison against known fields passes a threshold. Show image → extracted structured fields → validation. This is more visually interesting than code.

recipes.title: Prompt/workflow optimization
recipes.summary: Revise one prompt/workflow candidate using development feedback while retaining the frozen evaluation contract.
recipes.source_idea: Use a fixed evaluation set and iterate a prompt or agent workflow until the external evaluator crosses a target while cost/latency stays under bounds. The important part is that LoopExec evaluates against a frozen test set rather than accepting the model's own judgment. This is especially aligned with the product thesis.

inputs.name: max_cost_microusd

inputs.name: additional_constraints

Recorded latency and adapter/provider-enforced cost constraints satisfy the contract.

evidence: Observed invocation, latency and exact/unknown cost records

recipes.title: Cost-bounded agent workflow
recipes.summary: Reserve one permitted attempt before dispatch; after exhaustion request another only in an offline fixture to prove refusal.
recipes.source_idea: Let an agent try to solve a task under a strict model-call budget. Visually show remaining calls decreasing and LoopExec refusing a further call once the shared budget is exhausted. This is a great demo of the v0.4.x work because the “failure” itself is the proof.

inputs.name: scope_id
inputs.description: Existing or new explicit shared budget identity

inputs.name: phases
inputs.description: Builder/critic phases included in the allowance

inputs.name: additional_constraints
inputs.description: Optional additional user acceptance constraints; never replaces the required checks

recipes.attempt: Reserve one permitted attempt before dispatch; after exhaustion request another only in an offline fixture to prove refusal.
checks: Shared pre-call reservations never exceed max_calls across run IDs and phases.
A refused call never launches; failed launches retain consumed reservations.
Call-count bounds are not dollar bounds; strict monetary caps additionally require enforced per-call cost reservations.
protect: Shared scope identity, pinned allowance and append-only reservation history
evidence: Per-call reservations, remaining allowance and launch count
recipes.demo: Show remaining calls decrementing and an extra call being refused without launching.

recipes.title: Oscillation detection
recipes.summary: Produce the next alternating fixture state while retaining the same contradictory acceptance checks.
recipes.source_idea: Construct a deliberately pathological task where an agent alternates between A and B—perhaps formatting one file in mutually incompatible ways. LoopExec detects the repeated state and halts rather than looping forever. Visually this is excellent: A → B → A → B → oscillation_detected.

inputs.name: states
inputs.description: Deliberately conflicting states A and B

inputs.name: failure_ids
inputs.description: Stable failure identities for each state

inputs.name: additional_constraints
inputs.description: Optional additional user acceptance constraints; never replaces the required checks

recipes.attempt: Produce the next alternating fixture state while retaining the same contradictory acceptance checks.
checks: Repeated state/failure history produces the computed oscillation guard before the attempt/time cap.
The detector uses real captured observations and never a caller-supplied halt reason.
protect: Contradictory checks, failure identity mapping and detector policy
evidence: A/B state sequence and captured failure sets
recipes.demo: Animate A → B → A → B and the computed oscillation_detected stop.

recipes.title: Regression detection
recipes.summary: Fix one failing condition in the fixture while deliberately exposing a regression in a previously passing condition.
recipes.source_idea: Give a task with two acceptance conditions. The agent fixes one but breaks the other. LoopExec's ratchet catches that regression and refuses to count the iteration as progress. This may be one of the strongest conceptual demos because it exposes a very real agent failure mode.

inputs.name: conditions
inputs.description: At least two independently identified acceptance conditions

inputs.name: additional_constraints
inputs.description: Optional additional user acceptance constraints; never replaces the required checks

protect: Acceptance conditions, stable IDs and retained baseline evidence
evidence: Rejected candidate and restored-best identity when configured
recipes.demo: Show one check turn green while the other turns red, then the ratchet/restore result.
